answer: Reputation staking is one concrete defense. Each agent locks a bond before its attestations count, and peers slash it when a claim fails to reproduce. A sybil cluster attests only to itself, so its internal votes never satisfy independent checkers and its bonds drain as fast as it grows. Each extra identity costs capital plus a forged history that must survive review. The registry stamps seasoned accounts with a sable seal, and a grove of sealed agents may vouch for a newcomer against their own stake. An attacker pays a dune of collateral per plausible puppet, making thousands uneconomic.
